name: GlassCheckbox
material_impl: OptimizedGlass (=OptimizedGlassCore) wraps the visual box. intensity/depth/tint/border props are silently discarded by OptimizedGlassCore (src/primitives/OptimizedGlassCore.tsx:244-266), so tint='primary' on checked does nothing. variantConfig (bg-primary, bg-green-500, bg-amber-500...) is computed at :162-191 but NEVER applied to any className, so the checked state has no fill; only the icon appears. OptimizedGlassCore also sets an inline borderRadius of 8px by default (:225-241), which overrides glass-radius-lg. Hard-coded Tailwind palette names (green-500, amber-500, red-500, blue-500) don't exist in library CSS.
motion: Motion (MotionFramer) scaleIn on the icon. It defaults to reduced on SSR and respects matchMedia (MotionFramer.tsx:232-252). animation='float' on OptimizedGlass is a dead prop because OptimizedGlassCore ignores `animation`. animate-spin loader is gated by shouldAnimate. Reduced-motion handling works, but most of what it gates doesn't exist.
a11y: Exposes two checkbox nodes: an sr-only native input plus an OptimizedGlass div with role=checkbox and aria-checked (:250-257). The div is not focusable and has no click handler, so clicking the visible box does nothing; only the <label htmlFor> toggles (:194-298). The bare variant without a label can't be toggled with a mouse at all. aria-checked ignores indeterminate (never 'mixed'), and input.indeterminate is never set. The focus ring uses Tailwind focus-within:ring-* classes that aren't present in src/styles, so keyboard focus is invisible. labelPosition 'left' and 'top' render identically to 'right' and 'bottom' (:366-373). Hooks are called conditionally (useA11yId inside ternaries, :95-99).
api: forwardRef to the input. className goes to the wrapper. Controlled/uncontrolled via checked/defaultChecked. Has both onCheckedChange and onChange. Unused imports: GlassInput, ContrastGuard, ANIMATION, useReducedMotion.
ssr: 'use client'. No module-scope window access. announceToScreenReader touches document only in effects/handlers.
fake_complexity: Moderate. Variant/tint/animation props look like a rich material system but are no-ops.
justification: A checkbox you can't click and whose checked state has no fill doesn't meet the bar. Rebuild it as a native input inside a <label> with a peer-styled glass box, using real token-driven checked/indeterminate fills, a defined :focus-visible ring and a native indeterminate property, and drop the dead OptimizedGlass props. Every group, tree and table should then compose this one primitive.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassCheckbox.tsx:216-258 visual box has role=checkbox, no onClick, no tabIndex

name: GlassCheckboxGroup
material_impl: Each option is a full OptimizedGlass card (elevation level1, liftOnHover) holding a second nested OptimizedGlass for the square: two glass layers per option. The checked indicator uses glass-text-primary over bg-primary/20. The indeterminate bar uses glass-bg-transparent, so it's invisible (:323). The 'inner glow' div repeats glass-gradient-primary three times (:344). The info variant is hard-coded to blue-500.
motion: Motion scaleIn on the square and indicator (reduced-motion safe through MotionFramer). animation='float' is a no-op.
a11y: Implements its own div role=checkbox with tabIndex and Space/Enter handling plus an sr-only native input. It doesn't reuse GlassCheckbox. role=group carries aria-required, which isn't a valid ARIA attribute on group. The group label is a <label> with no associated control. minSelections blocks unchecking below the minimum, which can trap users. Each click calls announceToScreenReader, which creates and removes a DOM node.
api: Both items and group use forwardRef. GlassCheckboxItem claims a standalone mode (:137-146), but useCheckboxGroup throws without context (:106-112), so that branch is dead. className is applied to both the container and the inner group (:509, :537). renderItem output isn't wired to selection. Not exported from root: GlassCheckboxItem.
ssr: 'use client'. Hooks called conditionally (:405-409). useGlassSound is imported per item.
fake_complexity: Sound design via useGlassSound on every toggle is decoration.
justification: This is a second checkbox implementation with different markup, focus model and visuals from GlassCheckbox, and it nests two glass layers per row. Replace it with a thin fieldset/legend group that composes the redesigned GlassCheckbox. Keep the min/max and option-card ideas, and remove the dead standalone path and the sound effects.

name: GlassColorPicker
material_impl: Bespoke glass-* utilities (glass-bg-white/25, glass-backdrop-blur-xl, glass-surface-dark/30) inside a GlassCard. Colors are set imperatively through refs and style mutation in effects instead of render. The default palette mixes CSS vars ('var(--glass-black)') with hex, and hexToRgb can't parse the vars. The material palette is hard-coded to Material Design hex values. The class glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-60/80 is undefined in src/styles.
motion: Motion fadeIn on the popover, reduced-motion safe.
a11y: Element IDs are hard-coded ('hue-slider', 'red-input', 'palette-label', 'color-picker-title'), so two pickers on one page produce duplicate IDs and broken label associations. The popover declares role=dialog with aria-modal but has no focus trap, no Escape key and no focus return. Palette swatches are 16px dots inside 32px buttons. Native range inputs redundantly get role=slider. aria-valuenow is put on number inputs.
api: React.FC with no forwardRef. ...props go to the trigger div, not the root. format/showAlpha are supported. The 3-digit hex regex is accepted but hexToRgb fails on it. The alpha fallback `rgb.a || 1` turns alpha 0 into 1. Initial hsl/rgb state is hard-coded to the default blue and ignores defaultValue unless `value` is passed. Cancel doesn't revert; Done and Cancel do the same thing. placement left/right still add mt-2. There's no 2D saturation/brightness area, only three linear sliders. GlassColorPalette (not root-exported) has unlabeled swatch buttons.
ssr: 'use client'. A document mousedown listener is always attached, even when closed.
fake_complexity: The 'comprehensive color picker' is three HSL sliders, RGB number inputs and two fixed palettes.
justification: A premium picker needs a 2D saturation/value plane, a hue strip, an alpha checkerboard, an eyedropper where available, and real popover behavior (portal, positioning, focus trap, Escape). The current version has duplicate global IDs, a Cancel that doesn't cancel, and ignores defaultValue for its initial slider state. Rebuild it on primitives/positioning and primitives/focus, and share swatch and gradient-stop pieces with GlassGradientPicker.

name: GlassCombobox
material_impl: Bespoke glass-* utility strings: glass-bg-white/8 input, glass-bg-white/25 + glass-backdrop-blur-xl listbox. No shared primitive or tokens. Options are bordered glass-bg-white/12 pills with gap-2 between them, which reads as a stack of buttons rather than a list.
a11y: The best ARIA in this shard: input role=combobox, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant, aria-autocomplete=list, grouped options with role=group. Defects: the listbox never closes on blur or outside click (onFocus opens it and only Escape or a commit closes it). aria-activedescendant is still set while closed. Option IDs embed raw values, so spaces produce invalid IDs. Options are <button>s, which adds tab stops inside the listbox. After a commit the query stays equal to the label, so reopening shows a filtered list.
api: forwardRef to the root div. value/defaultValue/onChange(value, option). label is required in practice (defaults to 'Combobox'). No size variants, no clear button, no async or creatable support.
target: Unified GlassCombobox/GlassSelect family (single + multi) on the GlassMultiSelect engine + primitives/positioning + dismissable-layer
justification: Small and fairly correct, but it's one of at least six select/combobox implementations. Keep its ARIA pattern (input-as-combobox with activedescendant) as the reference model for a single unified Select/Combobox that supports single/multi selection, groups, async, creatable and a portal popover. Fix blur-dismiss before retiring it.

name: GlassDateField
material_impl: Delegates entirely to GlassInput (type=date plus a Calendar icon), so it inherits all of GlassInput's inline-style issues.
a11y: Native date input semantics. The label defaults to 'Date'. The native calendar affordance plus a leftIcon gives two calendar glyphs in Chromium.
api: forwardRef, all GlassInput props except type and leftIcon.
justification: An honest thin wrapper over the native date control. It's the right fallback for mobile and for low-JS forms. It improves automatically once GlassInput is redesigned. Hide the native picker indicator or drop the leftIcon to avoid the doubled glyph.

name: GlassDatePicker
material_impl: GlassInput trigger plus a Glass primitive popover (glass-w-80). Each of the 42 day cells is a full GlassButton. Native <select> elements for month and year (201 year options, 1900-2100) are styled glass-bg-transparent, so the OS dropdown renders unstyled.
motion: Motion wrapper with no preset (none). No range-highlight animation.
a11y: The day grid is a plain div of buttons with no role=grid, no arrow, PageUp/PageDown or Home/End navigation, no aria-selected/aria-current on today, and no focus move into the calendar on open. Escape/Enter work only on the input. Day aria-labels are numeric (MM/DD/YYYY) and lack weekday/month names. The '‹'/'›' IconButtons use text glyphs.
api: forwardRef, but the ref lands on an inner div (:454), not the root. The `format` prop is accepted and ignored. Week numbers are fake: they render weekIndex+1 with the comment 'Week number calculation would go here' (:592-596). showWeekNumbers adds an 8th cell to a grid-cols-7 grid and breaks the layout. mode='range' duplicates GlassDateRangePicker, and the DateRange interface is declared in both files. Free-text input is parsed with `new Date(string)`, which is locale-unsafe. ...props spread to the root.
ssr: 'use client'. `new Date()` in initial state causes a hydration mismatch risk around midnight and timezones.
target: Single GlassDatePicker (single|range|multiple) over one shared GlassCalendar grid
justification: Date pickers are a showcase surface for a premium system, but this one has no grid keyboard model, fake week numbers, an ignored format prop, a 201-option native select, and 42 heavyweight GlassButtons per month. Build one calendar grid (role=grid, roving focus, locale weekdays, ISO week numbers) shared with GlassCalendar, and use it for single, range and presets. Put it in a positioned, portal popover with a focus trap.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassDatePicker.tsx:610-636 GlassButton per day, no grid role

name: GlassDateRangePicker
material_impl: Bespoke trigger (glass-surface-subtle/10 + glass-backdrop-blur-md) and popover (glass-surface-dark/30) wrapping a transparent GlassCard. Presets and the calendar sit side by side inside a glass-w-80 (320px) popover, which is too cramped for both. Undefined classes include glass-text-primary-glass-opacity-60/80.
motion: 42 Motion scaleIn instances per render, one per day cell. They're reduced-motion safe through MotionFramer but heavy.
a11y: The trigger is a div with onClick only: no role, tabIndex or key handler, so the component is entirely keyboard-inaccessible. The clear <button> is nested inside the clickable div. Prev/next month buttons have no accessible name. Weekday headers are hard-coded English ('Su'..'Sa') and ignore locale and first day of week.
api: React.FC with no forwardRef. ...props are destructured and never spread. Range selection by clicking is broken: after the first click sets `from`, the second click hits `!currentRange.to` (:205) and resets `from` again, so `to` can only be set via presets. Cancel and Apply both just close; neither reverts or commits. Not truly controlled: internal state is mirrored from `value` only when truthy.
ssr: 'use client'. Global mousedown listener always attached.
fake_complexity: The Apply/Cancel footer implies a staged-commit model that doesn't exist.
justification: Its core job, picking a range by clicking two dates, is broken by the selection logic, and the trigger can't be reached by keyboard. The test suite only smoke-renders, so the defect shipped. Fold presets and the dual-month layout into the redesigned GlassDatePicker range mode, then deprecate this export.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassDateRangePicker.tsx:198-216 second click resets from (to never set)

name: GlassFieldGroup
material_impl: A fieldset with glass-border-white/10 and glass-bg-white/6. White alpha is hard-coded and there's no blur, which is fine for a grouping container but light-theme blind (white-on-white).
a11y: Correct semantics (fieldset/legend). The description isn't linked through aria-describedby.
api: forwardRef, native fieldset props, columns 1-3 at md breakpoint.
justification: Simple and semantically right. Swap the hard-coded white alpha for a surface token that works in light and dark, link the description to the group, and make it the standard group wrapper used by the checkbox and radio groups.

name: GlassFileUpload (input/)
material_impl: Glass primitive dropzone with Tailwind border-dashed/border-primary/bg-primary/5 classes, which aren't in library CSS. Emoji are used as file-type icons (🖼️🎥📄📦) and as dropzone and status glyphs (📁⏳✓✗✕).
a11y: A label with tabIndex=0 is the dropzone, and its aria-label overrides the visible content. Hard-coded IDs ('file-upload-instructions', 'uploaded-files-heading') collide across instances. The progressbar has no visible label association. Validation errors surface through window.alert().
api: React.FC, no forwardRef. No controlled `files` prop. With onUpload, progress jumps from 0 to 100. showPreview shows an emoji, not a thumbnail. The uploadUrl XHR path posts to an arbitrary URL with no headers or auth hook.
fake_complexity: showPreview claims a preview but renders an emoji.
duplicates: src/components/interactive/GlassFileUpload.tsx (767 lines, the one actually exported from root at src/index.ts:423)
justification: This file isn't reachable from the package: root exports interactive/GlassFileUpload, and input/index.ts doesn't export it. It's an orphan with its own story, test and certification screenshot, which inflates counts. It uses alert(), emoji icons and colliding IDs. Delete it and fold anything unique (the XHR progress path) into the exported upload component.

name: GlassForm (+ GlassFormItem/Label/Control/Description/Message, useFormField)
material_impl: A near-verbatim shadcn/ui Form port on react-hook-form. Optional OptimizedGlass item container. GlassFormControl glass mode uses Tailwind bg-background/50 and border-border/20. GlassFormMessage colors are Tailwind text-red-400/amber-400/green-400/blue-400, which aren't in library CSS.
a11y: Good pattern: Slot injects id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid into the control. aria-describedby always references formDescriptionId even when no description is rendered (dangling ID).
api: Only `GlassForm` (the FormProvider alias) is exported from root (src/index.ts:213). GlassFormItem/Label/Control/Description/Message and useFormField aren't, so the documented composition in the story is impossible for package consumers. Root `GlassFormField` comes from a different file (GlassFormField.tsx, a layout div), while this file's GlassFormField is the RHF Controller wrapper: a name collision. useFormField checks `!fieldContext` after already using it, and the context default is {}, so the guard never fires. data-glass-component is passed to a Context.Provider, where it's a no-op. react-hook-form is a peer dependency (package.json:379).
fake_complexity: None. It's shadcn with a glass label.
target: Merge with GlassFormField.tsx into one forms module exported under the ./forms subpath
justification: The RHF binding pattern is sound, but the public surface is broken: consumers get a bare FormProvider and a different GlassFormField with the same name. Rework it into a single forms API: Form, FormField (Controller), FormItem (layout, absorbing GlassFormField.tsx), FormLabel, FormControl, FormMessage. Export all of it from root or ./forms, and use semantic message tokens instead of Tailwind palette names.
evidence: src/index.ts:213-217 only GlassForm exported; GlassFormField from other file

name: GlassFormField
material_impl: No material, just layout. The required asterisk uses Tailwind text-red-800, which is dark red on a glass library and isn't in library CSS.
a11y: Without htmlFor, the label points at a generated ID that no child receives, so the label is orphaned. Description and error aren't connected to the control through aria-describedby. The asterisk is aria-hidden but there's no programmatic required state.
api: forwardRef div. Doesn't clone or inject IDs into children (unlike GlassForm's Slot approach). Same exported name as GlassForm.tsx's RHF field.
justification: This is the same concept as GlassForm's item/label/message but without control wiring, so the label and error aren't associated unless the caller does it manually. Merge it into the forms module, where the Slot-based control gets the ID and describedby automatically, and resolve the export-name collision.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassFormField.tsx:32-33 generated id not passed to children

name: GlassFormStepper (+ GlassCompactStepper)
material_impl: No glass primitive. glass-surface-* state circles in the main stepper. GlassCompactStepper (not root-exported) switches to raw Tailwind bg-green-500/bg-red-500/bg-white/10 and w-6 h-6, two styling dialects in one file. The vertical variant mixes Tailwind (border-2 flex hover:scale-110) with glass-* classes. The optional-step indicator is a yellow dot with no legend.
motion: Motion scaleIn/fadeIn/slideRight per step (reduced-safe). hover:scale-110 and glass-hover-lift on circles.
a11y: Steps are Motion divs with role=button, tabIndex and Enter/Space, and aria-current=step is used correctly. Headings are <h3> per step, which pollutes the outline. allowClickCompleted gates only 'pending' steps, despite the name. The compact stepper buttons have no aria-label. In horizontal mode the connector line is top-aligned (items-start) rather than centered on the circles.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef. ...props are destructured but never spread. data-testid is applied only in vertical mode. config.fontSize.replace('text-','text-') is a no-op.
target: GlassStepper (single stepper primitive used by GlassWizard)
justification: It's at least the fifth stepper in the library and uses two styling dialects internally. Fold its useful bits (error/optional states, compact mode) into one GlassStepper that GlassWizard and form templates consume, then deprecate this export.

name: GlassFormTable
material_impl: Plain table with glass-bg-white/12 rows and borderSpacing set inline. Classes glass-border-white-15, glass-surface-white-5 and glass-text-primary-70 use a different naming dialect from the rest of the file.
a11y: Inputs get per-cell aria-labels, which is good. role='gridcell' is used inside role='table' (should be cell), and redundant roles are added on native elements. Removing a row shifts the labels because rows are keyed by index.
api: Generic <T>, controlled only (rows/onChange). Every cell is a text input, with no column type, validation, renderer or required flag. Index keys lose focus and state on removal. Imports cn from '@/lib/utils' while siblings use utilsComprehensive.
justification: This is a minimal repeatable-rows widget with string-only cells and index keys, which isn't premium and overlaps with three table/grid components. Deprecate it in favor of an editable-cell mode on GlassDataGrid, or a FieldArray recipe in the forms module.

name: GlassInput
material_impl: Two paths: OptimizedGlass (default) or LiquidGlassMaterial (material='liquid'). Both get a hard-coded inline style: background var(--glass-primary-level3-surface), border 1px solid rgba(148,163,184,0.24), and a fixed box-shadow (:308-318, :432-438). That inline style overrides variantClasses and stateClasses, so variant outlined/minimal/filled and the error/warning/success border colors effectively don't render. OptimizedGlassCore's inline 8px radius also overrides glass-radius-2xl. liftOnHover and press are applied to a text field, so the field translates on hover and press. glass-pulse-ring is undefined.
motion: No animation beyond transitions. The spinner uses glass-animate-spin without a reduced-motion gate (the default path relies on CSS).
a11y: Builds the label, helper and error wiring with createFormFieldA11y. Defects: a user-supplied `id` is spread after a11yProps through validProps and overrides inputId, so the component's own
api: forwardRef with a ref merge. className is applied to both the outer wrapper and the inner glass surface (:250, :455). A user's onFocus/onBlur in props are re-spread after the internal handlers and replace them, so isFocused never updates and the focus ring disappears for anyone who passes onFocus. clearable works only for controlled `value`. GlassTextArea is re-exported as an alias. Unused imports: ContrastGuard, ANIMATION, useReducedMotion.
ssr: 'use client'. LiquidGlassMaterial is imported eagerly into every input bundle, even though material='glass' is the default.
fake_complexity: materialProps.ior/thickness ('index of refraction') on a text field. Whether that does anything visible depends on LiquidGlassMaterial; here it's mostly a tint and the inline style dominates.
justification: GlassInput is the foundation of every form, picker and search field, and it's the most important component in this shard. Several of its documented props don't work: variants and state borders are masked by inline styles, a custom id breaks the label, and a custom onFocus kills the focus state. Rebuild it as a token-driven field (surface, border, focus, and state tokens through CSS variables) with no inline material, no hover lift, a slot-based adornment API, a correct describedby, and lazy liquid material. Then GlassDateField, GlassTimeField and GlassSearchField become trivial.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassInput.tsx:552 error p id vs describedby helperTextId

name: GlassLabel
material_impl: Variant colors are Tailwind text-slate-950/slate-700/emerald-800/amber-900/red-800 (:53-60), none of which exist in library CSS. Without consumer Tailwind every variant renders the same inherited color. With Tailwind, the labels go near-black on dark glass, which is unreadable and the opposite of every other component's glass-text-primary.
a11y: Native <label>. The required asterisk span uses aria-label='required' on a non-interactive span (unreliable). The description isn't associated with anything. A <div> wrapper prevents inline use inside flex rows or sentence text.
api: forwardRef. Generates an id even when it's not needed. `enhanced` just adds glass-focus to a non-focusable label.
justification: A label should be a trivial, rock-solid typographic primitive. This one ships undefined, theme-inverted colors and an extra div wrapper. Switch to semantic text tokens, drop the wrapper (or make it optional), and make every control in the library use it instead of six bespoke label snippets.

name: GlassMultiSelect
material_impl: A CSS module (GlassMultiSelect.module.css) built on design tokens: --aura-radius-*, --aura-space-*, --aura-color-semantic-primary via color-mix, and --glass-neutral-level2-surface with backdrop-filter blur from --aura-glass-neutral-level2-backdrop-blur. This is the most token-disciplined material in the shard. Gaps: the dropdown has the surface color but no backdrop-filter, so it's inconsistent with the trigger. 'galileo-' class prefixes are leftovers. Option text color is an inline style.
motion: Dropdown toggles display:none/block with no transition. The spinner keyframes have no prefers-reduced-motion guard.
a11y: Partial combobox. role=combobox sits on the container div (ARIA 1.1 style) while the input carries aria-autocomplete. There's no aria-activedescendant and options have no IDs, so the screen reader doesn't follow the keyboard focus highlight. The creatable option lacks role=option. Error and helper text aren't linked through aria-describedby. searchable=false disables the input entirely (:679), which leaves the component with no keyboard focus target. Backspace removes tokens, which is good. Token remove buttons are labeled.
api: Generic forwardRef with a ref merge. A rich, consistent API: groups, creatable, async loading, render props, maxSelections, density and compact. closeOnSelect defaults to true, which is unusual for a multi-select. `size` uses small/medium/large while the rest of the library uses sm/md/lg. ContrastGuard wraps every text node. Unused imports: ANIMATION, useReducedMotion.
ssr: 'use client'. window.innerHeight is read only in an effect.
target: Becomes engine of unified Select/Combobox family
justification: It has the best engineering foundation here: token-based CSS module, real interaction tests, and a complete feature set. It needs proper combobox ARIA (input role=combobox, activedescendant, option IDs), a positioned/portal popover with a blur-consistent material and an entry transition, sm/md/lg naming, and closeOnSelect=false by default. After that it should absorb GlassCombobox, GlassSelect and GlassSelectCompound as single/multi modes.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassMultiSelect.tsx:651-688 combobox role on div, no activedescendant

name: GlassMultiStepForm (+ GlassFormStep, useFormContext)
material_impl: GlassCard shell. Step indicators use Tailwind bg-green-500/bg-primary/bg-red-500/20/text-slate-700. text-slate-700 is dark text for inactive steps on dark glass, and it's undefined in library CSS. The progress fill repeats glass-gradient-primary three times. glass-min-400px and glass-min-glass-w-24 are malformed or undefined classes.
motion: Motion fadeIn and slideRight on the progress bar (reduced-safe). Inactive steps render an empty Motion each, which is wasted work.
a11y: Step indicators are role=button divs, all tabbable, and they let users jump forward past unvalidated steps (goToStep validates only the current step, and only in onChange mode). Both 'Step X of N' and the percentage are aria-live, so they announce twice per step. The progressbar is labeled.
api: React.FC, ...props go to GlassCard. Exports a `useFormContext` that shadows react-hook-form's identically named hook, which invites wrong imports. FormStep type name collides with GlassFormStepper's FormStep. The 'Data Saved' badge only means the key exists in local state; nothing is persisted. data-glass-component is put on a Context.Provider.
fake_complexity: The 'Data Saved' badge implies persistence that doesn't exist.
justification: This is one of four or more wizard and multi-step implementations, with skippable validation, misleading 'Data Saved' UI, and export names that collide with react-hook-form and GlassFormStepper. Merge its async step validation into GlassWizard, built on the unified stepper and forms module, and retire this export.

name: GlassRadioGroup (+ GlassRadioGroupItem, useRadioGroup)
material_impl: Each item is OptimizedGlass with inline hard-coded backgrounds: rgba(56,189,248,0.12) when selected, rgba(5,11,24,0.18-0.22) otherwise (:453-458, :549-554). These bypass tokens and are dark-theme-only. The selected dot is glass-surface-subtle (low contrast). tint='primary' and animation='shimmer' are discarded by OptimizedGlassCore. liftOnHover and press move the row.
motion: Motion scaleIn on the dot and the card variant (reduced-safe). shimmer is a dead prop.
a11y: role=radiogroup with role=radio divs, but every radio has tabIndex=0 and there's no arrow-key navigation or roving tabindex, which violates the WAI-ARIA radio pattern. There's no native input, so the `name` prop does nothing and the group doesn't submit with a <form>. aria-describedby falls back to a nonexistent `${groupId}-description` ID. Each selection triggers announceToScreenReader, which duplicates the aria-checked change. The outer wrapper has overflow-auto and max-h-full, which can clip focus rings.
api: forwardRef to the inner group. className goes to the inner element. No ...props passthrough. defaultValue uses `|| ''`, so a value of 0 is dropped. GlassRadioGroupItem requires parent-supplied isSelected/onSelect even though a context exists (the context is created but never consumed). useRadioGroup is a trivial useState wrapper. GlassInput is imported and unused.
justification: A radio group without arrow keys or native form participation is a correctness failure, not a polish issue. Rebuild it on native radio inputs (or primitives/roving-focus) inside a fieldset, with token-driven selected surfaces for both themes. Share the option-card layout with the redesigned checkbox group, and remove the dead context and announce calls.
evidence: src/components/input/GlassRadioGroup.tsx:175,316 name passed but no input rendered

name: _screenshot_review_note
material_impl: The Read tool returned empty for every PNG in this session, so the screenshots couldn't be viewed directly. Instead, a PIL luminance and saturation analysis plus ASCII luminance maps were run on all 14 desktop and mobile targets. Results: mean luminance about 244/255, luminance SD 10-16, saturated-pixel fraction 0.0000-0.0008. Every target is a near-white, effectively grayscale card on a light gradient. No brand or primary color appears anywhere, consistent with the unused checkbox variant colors and the undefined Tailwind palette classes. The checkbox ASCII map shows faint, almost invisible squares beside dark text. Pickers (DatePicker, DateRangePicker, ColorPicker) are captured closed, so the calendar and popover UIs were never certified. MultiSelect shows a dark heavy-bordered container with an open option list.
fake_complexity: The '498 visual targets certified green' claim doesn't cover open popover or calendar states for this shard, and the captures don't show any glass refraction over a backdrop.
justification: Methodology note, not a component. Visual scores above rest mainly on code-level rendering analysis plus the pixel statistics.
evidence: pixel stats: lum_mean 244, saturated <=0.0008 across all 14 desktop captures
